importance.reason: Dynamic planar nearest-neighbor searching is a basic geometric data-structure problem.

sentences: Maintain a changing set of planar points while answering exact Euclidean nearest-neighbor queries.
The target is logarithmic time for insertions, deletions, and queries within one data structure.
Deleting a point can expose many previously hidden candidates, making fully dynamic maintenance harder than static searching.
The source also relates the problem to dynamic convex hulls in three dimensions.
Achieving the target would extend the efficiency of ordinary ordered search to planar proximity without rebuilding a global geometric structure after updates.
